paragraphs.title: The First Attempt to Bring Up the Ark and Uzzah's Death

easy.explanation: David gathered thirty thousand chosen men of Israel.
easy.q: How many chosen men of Israel did David gather?

easy.explanation: They went to bring up the ark of God.
easy.q: What did David and the people seek to bring up?

easy.explanation: Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark.
easy.q: Who took hold of the ark when the oxen shook it?

medium.explanation: The ark of God was set upon a new cart.
medium.q: How was the ark transported during the first attempt?

answers: Because the people wanted to hide it
medium.explanation: Uzzah took hold of the ark because the oxen shook it.
medium.q: Why did Uzzah reach out his hand to the ark?

answers: The oxen caused the ark to be shaken or unsteady
The oxen ran away from the cart
medium.explanation: The statement means that the oxen made the ark shake or become unsteady.
medium.q: What does “the oxen shook it” mean in this passage?

challenge.explanation: God smote Uzzah there, and he died by the ark of God.
challenge.q: What happened after Uzzah touched the ark?

challenge.explanation: David called the name of the place Perez-uzzah.
challenge.q: What name did David give the place because of this event?

answers: He was afraid and did not want to bring the ark to him
He decided to leave the ark on the cart
challenge.explanation: David was afraid and asked, “How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?”
challenge.q: How did the event affect David?

paragraphs.title: The Ark in the House of Obed-edom

easy.explanation: David carried the ark aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
easy.q: To whose house was the ark taken?

easy.explanation: The ark continued in his house three months.
easy.q: How long did the ark remain in the house of Obed-edom?

easy.explanation: The LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
easy.q: What did the LORD do for Obed-edom and all his household?

answers: He was afraid because of what had happened to Uzzah
There was no room in the city
medium.explanation: David was afraid of the LORD after Uzzah's death.
medium.q: Why was David unwilling at first to bring the ark into the City of David?

answers: He heard that the LORD had blessed Obed-edom's house
medium.explanation: David heard that the LORD had blessed the house of Obed-edom.
medium.q: What caused David to change his decision?

answers: David moved or redirected the ark
medium.explanation: David moved the ark to the house of Obed-edom.
medium.q: What does “David carried it aside” mean here?

answers: At first there is fear, but at the end there is blessing
At first there is blessing, but at the end there is war
At first there is silence, but at the end there is mourning
challenge.explanation: David is afraid of the ark, but the ark brings blessing to Obed-edom's house.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the beginning and end of this passage?

answers: The ark will remain there forever
David will bring the ark up with gladness
challenge.explanation: After hearing of the blessing, David brings the ark into the City of David with gladness.
challenge.q: What does the blessing of Obed-edom's house suggest about what happens next?

challenge.explanation: It was told king David that the LORD had blessed the house of Obed-edom.
challenge.q: Who was told about the blessing of Obed-edom's house?

paragraphs.title: Bringing the Ark to the City of David with Joy

easy.explanation: When the bearers had gone six paces, David sacrificed oxen and fatlings.
easy.q: After how many paces did the bearers sacrifice?

easy.explanation: David was girded with a linen ephod.
easy.q: What was David wearing while he danced before the LORD?

answers: In the tabernacle David had prepared
easy.explanation: The ark was set in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it.
easy.q: Where was the ark placed in the City of David?

answers: They sacrificed, shouted, and played music
They left the City of David
medium.explanation: They brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.
medium.q: What did David and the people do while bringing up the ark?

answers: He returned the ark to Obed-edom
medium.explanation: David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
medium.q: What did David do after offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings?

medium.explanation: The word describes a loud and joyful sound made during the procession.
medium.q: What does “shouting” mean in the context of this procession?

answers: At first it was transported on a cart, but later it was carried by bearers
At first it was in a tent, but later it was in a house
At first there were no people, but later there was no ark
challenge.explanation: The first attempt used a new cart, while the later procession had bearers carrying the ark.
challenge.q: What was the main difference between the first attempt and the later bringing of the ark to Jerusalem?

answers: He enthusiastically joined in worship before the LORD
He hid himself from the people
challenge.explanation: David danced before the LORD with all his might.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David's behavior during the procession?

answers: To all the people, both women and men
Only to the bearers of the ark
challenge.explanation: David gave food to the whole multitude of Israel, including women and men.
challenge.q: To whom did David distribute food after the ark arrived?

short_answers.question: What kind of ephod did David wear?
short_answers.explanation: David was girded with a linen ephod.

short_answers.question: What instrument sounded as the ark was brought up?
short_answers.explanation: The people brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.

short_answers.question: What did David offer before the LORD?
short_answers.explanation: David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

easy.explanation: Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David.
easy.q: Who saw David leaping and dancing before the LORD?

answers: She despised him in her heart
easy.explanation: Michal despised David in her heart.
easy.q: How did Michal respond to David's behavior?

answers: She had no child until the day of her death
easy.explanation: The passage says that Michal had no child until the day of her death.
easy.q: What does the final verse say about Michal?

answers: Failing to bring up the ark
Uncovering himself and behaving shamefully before the people
medium.explanation: Michal mocked David for uncovering himself before the handmaids of his servants.
medium.q: What did Michal accuse David of doing?

answers: He was rejoicing before the LORD
He was trying to escape from the people
medium.explanation: David said that his actions were before the LORD, who had chosen him.
medium.q: How did David explain his behavior?

medium.explanation: Michal claimed that David had exposed himself in the eyes of the handmaids.
medium.q: What does “uncovered himself” mean in Michal's complaint?

answers: David sees the dancing as rejoicing before the LORD, while Michal sees it as shameful
David wants to return the ark, while Michal wants to bring it up
David fears the people, while Michal blesses him
challenge.explanation: David views his actions as worship before the LORD, but Michal mocks and despises him.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between David and Michal in this passage?

answers: He is willing to humble himself for the LORD's honor
He is more important than all the people
He has no connection with worship
challenge.explanation: David says he will be more vile and base in his own sight before the LORD.
challenge.q: What does David emphasize about his position before the LORD?

answers: It explains that he sees himself as chosen to rule God's people and therefore rejoices before the LORD
It proves that he wants to leave the kingdom
It shows that he opposed bringing up the ark
challenge.explanation: David recalls that the LORD chose him to be ruler over Israel, which explains his joyful worship.
challenge.q: Why is David's mention of his choosing important to his answer to Michal?
